les: Marco Polo vat die pad na die Ooste
kaps_punt: Europese ontdekkingsreisiger Marco Polo en sy reise

items.bewering: Speserye het lank voor Marco Polo se tyd op Europa se markte beland.
items.bron: J. H. Munro, review of P. Freedman, Out of the East: Spices and the Medieval Imagination, American Historical Review, April 2009 (https://www.economics.utoronto.ca/munro5/MunroFreedmanAHR09.pdf): Europeans 'and the Romans before them' kept a steady demand for spices; the Roman pepper trade with India is also described at https://www.worldhistory.org/Pepper/ and in De Romanis, The Indo-Roman Pepper Trade and the Muziris Papyrus (Oxford).

items.bewering: Min mense in Europa het geweet waar daardie speserye groei. Die pad daarheen het deur lande geloop wat min Europeërs self gesien het.
items.bron: Munro on Freedman, AHR 2009 (https://www.economics.utoronto.ca/munro5/MunroFreedmanAHR09.pdf): medieval Europe linked spices with a 'distant, mysterious' East and with Paradise, told tales of spices guarded by serpents, and bought them through Muslim and other Asian middlemen.

items.bewering: Marco Polo was 'n handelaar uit die hawestad Venesië. In sy stad het skepe en handelaars van ver af gekom en gegaan.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo (Venetian merchant; his father traded with the Near East; he learnt to handle cargo ships); https://archive.aramcoworld.com/issue/200504/the.explorer.marco.polo.htm (he grew up in a Venetian merchant family); Munro, AHR 2009 (Venice as a spice-trading centre dealing with Alexandria and Beirut).

items.bewering: Hy het self oor land na Asië gereis en later vertel wat hy gesien het.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo: the Polos first SAILED from Venice to Acre on the coast of the eastern Mediterranean, which is already in Asia, and only from there went on overland along the Silk Road to Kublai Khan's court. The leg from Europe to Asia was by sea; the overland part was the journey THROUGH Asia. The second half of the sentence (he later told what he saw) is correct.
items.regstelling: Say that the overland part was the journey through Asia, not the way from Europe to Asia. For example: he first sailed to the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea and then travelled overland through Asia; or 'Hy het self die lang pad deur Asië oor land afgelê en later vertel wat hy gesien het.' This keeps the contrast with the return journey, which went mostly by sea (see 'Terug in Venesië').

items.bewering: Ons noem iemand wat so reis en dan daaroor vertel, 'n ontdekkingsreisiger.
items.bron: Vocabulary.com, Dutch 'ontdekkingsreiziger': 'someone who travels into little known regions' (https://www.vocabulary.com/dictionary/nl/ontdekkingsreiziger); Inburgering.org gives 'explorer' with Marco Polo as its example (https://inburgering.org/nl/de-of-het/ontdekkingsreiziger). 'So reis' refers back to travel through lands few Europeans had seen, which matches the core meaning; reporting back is part of what explorers do, though not strictly part of the definition.

items.bewering: Reisigers het in daardie tyd saam met handelskaravane oor land gereis.
items.bron: National Geographic, 'Marco Polo in China' (https://www.nationalgeographic.com/history/article/marco-polo-in-china-archival): 'the small caravan of Marco Polo' crossing from the Pamirs c. 1274-75; UNESCO Silk Roads, caravanserais that hosted merchants and their caravans (https://fr.unesco.org/silkroad/node/8325).

items.bewering: 'n Karavaan was 'n groep handelaars en diere wat saam op pad was. Saam was hulle veiliger as 'n handelaar wat alleen gereis het.
items.bron: Dictionary.com: a caravan is 'a group of travelers, as merchants or pilgrims, journeying together for safety in passing through deserts, hostile territory, etc.'; Encyclopaedia Britannica (historical editions, via jimclifford.ca): travellers 'especially merchants' marching together for mutual protection. In this block the sentence is about trade caravans ('handelskaravane'), so limiting it to traders is fair here. See the 'karavaan' glossary item for the same wording read on its own.

items.bewering: Die pad het oor droë woestyne en oor hoë berge geloop.
items.bron: Museo Galileo, Fra Mauro exhibition, 'Second voyage of Niccolò, Matteo and Marco Polo' (https://mostre.museogalileo.it/framauro/en/cosmography-and-sources/merchants-and-travelers/second-voyage-niccolo-matteo-and-marco-polo.html): the Polos crossed the Pamir range and the Tarim Basin (Kashgar, Khotan, Lop) and then the Gobi Desert; National Geographic (above): the track down from 'the snowbound heights of the Pamir'.

items.bewering: Die karavaan het van die een handelsplek na die volgende beweeg. By elke plek kon die mense rus en water en kos kry.
items.bron: UNESCO Silk Roads, 'Caravanserais: cross-roads of commerce and culture along the Silk Roads' (https://fr.unesco.org/silkroad/node/8325): stopping places on the inland routes where merchants and caravans rested and prepared for the next leg, and where trade was done.

items.bewering: So 'n reis het maande geduur en soms selfs jare.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo: the Polos were welcomed at Kublai's summer palace 'three and a half years after leaving Venice'.

items.bewering: Marco Polo het jare lank in Asië gebly.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo: about 24 years away (1271-1295), 17 of them in the Khan's lands; Aramco World (above): served Kublai Khan for 17 years.

items.bewering: Sy verhale is later in 'n boek opgeteken.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo: written down with Rustichello da Pisa while both were prisoners in Genoa, usually dated 1298-1299, after his return in 1295.

items.bewering: Die boek vertel dat hy tyd by die hof van 'n magtige heerser deurgebring het. Hy het van die stede, die handel en die gebruike van daardie plekke geleer.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo: the book describes his time in the service of Kublai Khan and the cities, trade and customs of Yuan China and the lands along the route.

items.bewering: Handel het ook daar mense en goedere oor groot afstande laat beweeg.
items.bron: UNESCO Silk Roads (https://fr.unesco.org/silkroad/node/8325); Aramco World (above): merchant ships from southern China visiting Malabar ports; Munro, AHR 2009: goods moved from eastern and southern Asia to Alexandria over long and dangerous distances.

items.bewering: Mense in Europa het min geweet van baie dinge wat hy vertel het. [read as a set with the list 'Wat die boek van Asië vertel']
items.bron: Read as a set with the four list items, as the brief asked. Each item is something the book tells, and each fits 'Europe knew little of it'. (1) Paper money: Europe had no banknotes until Stockholm in 1661 (Cité de l'Économie, Banque de France, https://www.citeco.fr/10000-years-history-economics/antiquity-to-middle-ages/the-first-banknotes-or-paper-money). (2) Huge Chinese cities: Hangzhou, close to a million people under the Song, against a few tens of thousands to about a hundred thousand in the largest European cities. (3) Where spices grew: wrapped in legend in Europe (Munro on Freedman, AHR 2009). (4) A state relay post: the Mongol yam is listed among the things European travellers described 'in great detail' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yam_(route)). The sentence says 'baie dinge', not 'everything', so it does not claim Europe knew nothing of each one, and the set does not overreach.

items.bewering: Papiergeld wat mense gebruik het in plaas van munte van metaal.
items.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo: Polo's description of Yuan paper money (the shape and size of the paper, the use of seals) is among the details judged authentic; Polo's chapter on the Khan's paper money, made from mulberry bark and stamped with his seal, says it is used for payments throughout his lands (summarised at https://finclusion.substack.com/p/paper-money-and-marco-polo and https://www.citeco.fr/10000-years-history-economics/antiquity-to-middle-ages/the-first-banknotes-or-paper-money).

items.bewering: Stede wat baie groter was as dié wat hy in Europa geken het.
items.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
items.bron: Columbia University, Asia for Educators, 'Song Dynasty China: Hangzhou' (https://afe.easia.columbia.edu/songdynasty-module/cities-hangzhou.html): Polo calls Kinsay (Hangzhou) 'beyond dispute the finest and the noblest in the world', about 'a hundred miles of compass', with ten main markets each drawing 40,000-50,000 people on market days. Hangzhou grew to almost a million people under the Song, far beyond any European city of the time, Venice included. This is a comparative, not a superlative, and it holds both as a report of the book and in fact.

items.bewering: Plekke waar speserye gekweek is.
items.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
items.bron: Aramco World, 'The Explorer Marco Polo' (https://archive.aramcoworld.com/issue/200504/the.explorer.marco.polo.htm): on the Malabar coast of India Polo marvelled at 'the immense production of pepper, cinnamon, ginger and other spices'. He also gave Java as a source of pepper, cloves and nutmeg, which is partly wrong (those came from the Moluccas), but the lesson claims only that the book describes places where spices were grown, and Malabar is such a place.

items.bewering: Ruiters wat briewe aangegee het, elkeen net tot by die volgende stilhouplek.
items.blok: Wat die boek van Asië vertel
items.bron: Polo's own text, Yule translation, chapter on the Kaan's posts and runners (Project Gutenberg text via https://www.bookrags.com/ebooks/10636/652.html): when those at the next post hear the bells, they get ready 'another horse and a man equipt in the same way, and he takes over the letter or whatever it be, and is off full-speed to the third station'. So the despatch passes from rider to rider at each station. The same chapter has foot-runners relaying every three miles. Also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yam_(route): 'A messenger would arrive at a station and give his information to another messenger.'

items.bewering: Ná baie jare het Marco Polo die pad terug na Venesië gevat. Die terugreis het langs 'n ander roete geloop as die reis daarheen.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo: around 1292 they sailed from Zaitun (Quanzhou) via Sumatra and southern India to Hormuz, then went overland to Trebizond, and were back in Venice in 1295; the outward journey had gone overland along the Silk Road. Aramco World (above): he sailed home through the China Sea, the Malacca Strait and the Indian Ocean.

items.bewering: Ons weet van sy reise omdat sy verhale in die boek opgeteken is. Daardie boek is die bron waaruit byna al ons kennis van sy reise kom. Sonder daardie boek sou ons byna niks van sy reise geweet het nie.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo: the other surviving documents (a 1305 tax record, his uncle Maffeo's testament, his own will) concern his life in Venice, not the journey, and almost nothing is known of him apart from the book. 'Byna al' and 'byna niks' are correctly hedged; an unhedged 'al' or 'niks' would not be, because Yuan and Persian records independently confirm the bride-escort mission his book describes.

items.bewering: Die boek is met die hand gekopieer, want Europa het toe nog nie drukperse gehad nie.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo: about 150 manuscript copies survive and the original is lost; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johannes_Gutenberg: printing press working in Europe by about 1450, some 150 years after the book (1298-99); Aramco World (above) shows a 1477 printed edition, the first print came long after the manuscripts.

items.bewering: Die kopieë verskil van mekaar, en party vertel 'n deel anders as ander.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo: 'During copying and translating many errors were made, so there are many differences between the various copies'; versions in Franco-Italian, Old French, Tuscan, Venetian and Latin.

items.bewering: Historici aanvaar daarom nie elke deel van die boek as vasstaande feit nie. Party dele pas by wat ons uit ander bronne weet. Ander dele kan nie in enige ander bron nagegaan word nie.
items.bron: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo: 'Many of the details in Polo's accounts have been verified' (e.g. the Christian churches at Zhenjiang and salt revenues matching Yuan documents), while critics question other parts, and Rustichello may have glamorised it; Elvin speaks of 'the ultimately overwhelming probability of the broad authenticity'. The universal 'enige' attaches only to 'ander dele' (some parts), which is correct: no Chinese record names Polo, so his own role at court rests on the book alone.

items.bewering: 'n Mens mag 'n bron bevraagteken sonder om hom heeltemal weg te gooi.
items.bron: A statement of historical method, not a fact claim. It matches how historians treat this very book: doubts about some parts sit beside acceptance of 'broad authenticity' (Elvin, cited at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travels_of_Marco_Polo).

items.bewering: In dieselfde tydperk as Mapungubwe het Marco Polo in Asië gereis.
items.bron: World History Encyclopedia, 'Mapungubwe' (https://www.worldhistory.org/Mapungubwe/): flourished from the 11th to the 13th century, 'already in decline by the late 13th century'; the hill capital is usually dated c. 1220 to c. 1290/1300. Polo was in Asia 1271-1295 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo). The periods overlap from 1271 to about 1290.

items.bewering: Die twee plekke lê baie ver van mekaar af. Ons plaas hulle langs mekaar omdat hulle in een tydperk bestaan het.
items.bron: Geography: the Limpopo valley in southern Africa against Yuan China and Central Asia, many thousands of kilometres apart; the periods overlap as in the item above.

items.bewering: Marco Polo het nie na Mapungubwe gereis nie. Sy boek vertel ook niks van daardie koninkryk nie.
items.bron: Polo's African chapters (Book Third) deal only with Madagascar, Zanzibar, Abyssinia and Aden, all from hearsay (contents of Yule's translation, Project Gutenberg vol. 2, https://gutenberg.org/cache/epub/12410/pg12410-images.html). World History Encyclopedia (above): no written records of Mapungubwe survive from the period, and its history is 'pieced together from archaeological finds only'.

items.bewering: Handel was op albei plekke 'n belangrike rede waarom mense sulke lang reise onderneem het. By Mapungubwe het handel die koninkryk ryk en sterk gemaak.
items.bron: UNESCO nomination document (https://whc.unesco.org/document/151741): gold and ivory, with access to the East African coast to trade with Arab, Indian and Chinese traders; Chinese porcelain and glass beads at the site. World History Encyclopedia (above): long-distance exchange brought wealth to the ruling elite and probably strengthened political control; it calls Mapungubwe a 'kingdom' and 'perhaps southern Africa's first state'. The Polos travelled as merchants (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Polo).

items.bewering: 'n Ontdekkingsreisiger is iemand wat na plekke reis wat sy eie mense nog nie ken nie, en wat dan vertel wat hy daar gesien het.
items.bron: Vocabulary.com, 'someone who travels into little known regions'; mijnwoordenboek.nl, 'a person who explores unknown regions' (see the first ontdekkingsreisiger item). 'Plekke wat sy eie mense nog nie ken nie' matches 'little known / unknown regions'. 'Vertel' is an addition to the dictionary sense but not a false one.

items.bewering: 'n Karavaan is 'n groep handelaars, diere en goedere wat saam op reis is.
items.bron: Dictionary.com: 'a group of travelers, as merchants or pilgrims, journeying together for safety'; Encyclopaedia Britannica (historical editions): a body of travellers, 'often pilgrims and especially merchants'. A caravan is defined by people travelling together with pack animals, for safety. Traders are the most common case, but not the definition: pilgrim caravans, such as those to Mecca, are caravans too. Read on its own, as glossary entries are, this entry says a caravan IS a group of traders, which is too narrow to be a true definition. The study block's sentence is fine because it is about trade caravans.
items.regstelling: Widen the subject from traders to travellers, keeping traders as the main example. For example: ''n Karavaan is 'n groep reisigers, dikwels handelaars, wat saam met hul diere en goedere reis.' Keeping the safety idea ('...wat vir veiligheid saam reis') would match the dictionaries even better, if there is room.

items.bewering: 'n Heerser se hof is die plek waar hy woon en regeer, met sy helpers om hom.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster 'court' (https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/court, via search): 'the residence or establishment of a sovereign', 'the family and retinue of a sovereign', 'the sovereign and officers and advisers who are the governing power'.

items.bewering: 'n Bron is iets waaruit ons kan leer - 'n foto, 'n geskrif, 'n storie, 'n onderhoud of 'n voorwerp - oor nou of oor lank gelede.
items.bron: Universität des Saarlandes course slides, 'Historical Sources' (https://www.coli.uni-saarland.de/courses/tm-hist11/slides/HistoricalSources.pdf): 'all texts, objects or facts that give us information about the past'; library guides (https://libguides.pace.edu/primary_sources, https://csulb.libanswers.com/faq/30658) list photographs, written documents, oral interviews and objects as source types. 'Oor nou' widens it beyond history to sources in general, which is true.

items.bewering: Historici is mense wat die geskiedenis ondersoek en daaroor skryf.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'historian' (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/historian): 'A writer of history'; 'One who studies or researches history.'

opsomming: Two items, both easy to fix, send this back to the writer. The lesson says Marco Polo travelled 'oor land na Asië', but he first sailed from Venice to Acre and only then went overland through Asia. The 'karavaan' glossary entry defines a caravan as a group of traders, which is too narrow, because pilgrim caravans count too. Everything else checks out. That includes reading the list 'Wat die boek van Asië vertel' together with the sentence about how little Europe knew: all four items appear in Polo's book, including the relay riders handing letters on at each station, and none overreaches. The lesson has no superlatives or analogies that fail; its 'byna al' and 'enige ander bron' are correctly hedged.
